THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key), and `doneRecent`
(iter151, drained to empty because every entry was already in done-archive.jsonl - see
`doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.

M6 feature-complete. **ITER157 SWEPT ALL SEVEN OPEN DECISIONS FOR THE EMBEDDED FACTUAL HOMEWORK ITER156's METHOD LOOKS FOR — THE SWEEP nextAction ASKED FOR IS NOW DONE — AND SHIPPED THE ONE FINDING WITH A TESTABLE CONSEQUENCE. Nothing was decided; three decision bodies gained facts.**

  (1) **planSection5Deviations: the promise surface is SIX shipped files per dead knob, not the three recorded, and TWO skills name `links.repoBlobUrl`, not one.** The unrecorded places are `plugin/skills/docs-loop/SKILL.md:60` and `plugin/skills/docs-refresh/SKILL.md:44` — 'Inputs, read in this order' tables, and docs-refresh's lists BOTH dead knobs as `docume.json` fields the skill reads, so an agent is told twice that a field doing nothing is an input. `DeadFields[0].Why`, this file and the archive all said to strike it from §6.2 'and the skill', SINGULAR, for 34 iterations. src/ mentions neither knob (0/0), which cross-checks the reader analysis.

  (2) **planSection6Deviations: nothing shipped depends on the three unbuilt §6 options** — no artifact passes `--verbose`, every `--json` hangs off `status` where it IS built, `--offline` is built, PLAN.md:363 correctly spells `drift --format json`. 'Correct §6' breaks no consumer; 'build them' unblocks nothing asking.

  (3) **m5Acceptance: option (a) is confirmed zero-secret, and option (b)'s stated cost was OVERSTATED** — docs-publish.yml is push-to-main FILTERED TO `paths:['docs/wiki/**']`, not every push, and docs-refresh.yml is not push-triggered at all (cron + workflow_dispatch).

  **SHIPPED: `PlanDataContractTests.Every_shipped_artifact_that_names_a_dead_knob_is_recorded`**, pinning each knob's `Places` in BOTH directions so a half-strike is loud instead of silent. 3/3 mutations: partial strike CAUGHT, seventh place CAUGHT, a mention in dated `docs/plans/` correctly OK-IGNORED (that exclusion is structural — the walk roots at `docs/wiki`, not `docs`).

  **THE NEAR-MISS WORTH READING BEFORE THE NEXT SWEEP: the gap iter157 first hypothesised DOES NOT EXIST.** The shipped SKILL.md files' `docume` invocations looked unguarded because SkillContractTests has no such check; `CliReferencePageTests.Every_documented_invocation_names_a_real_command_with_real_options` already sweeps ~132 invocations tree-wide including every SKILL.md and workflow template. A class named after `cli.md` owns a tree-wide sweep, and the duplicate test was nearly written. Asking what DIMENSION that sweep covers (CLI options, NOT config-field promises) is what found the real gap. Lesson in method-notes.md.

  Verified: build 0/0; run-suite.py **1388/1388 at HEAD before any write and 1389/1389 after** (+1 = the new test); PlanDataContractTests 5/5; the mutation harness left the tree clean. **The iter154 flake did not reproduce; it is still unnamed, and that is still the honest state.**
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE. USE run-suite.py, NOT `dotnet test | tail`** (iter154): `tail` keeps the summary and drops the failure lines above it, so a red suite becomes a bare number. It leaves a log + TRX in `.mtk/suite-runs/` (gitignored), prints failing ids with their assertion messages, drops the artifacts on green, mirrors the exit code, and takes `--repeat N` for a flake hunt. Several tests sweep the tree's own prose (RepositorySlugTests over `*.md`/`*.yml`/`*.json` outside `tests/` and `tools/`, QuickstartTests over fenced commands), so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1**; plain `dotnet test` is the command. One class is `dotnet test --filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, **ONE pattern only** (`a|b` exits 1, `(a|b)` exits 8, `--treenode-filter` is dead — iter143). Expect **1389** tests, not 1388.

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`. AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** — that is how iter155 found `decisions.formatOnEditHook`. **Trust the `decisions` and `gates` fields plus GATES.md's checkboxes over any prose in `phase`/`nextAction`**, which are written an iteration earlier and go stale the moment Mirko replies.

**THE DECISION SWEEP IS FINISHED — DO NOT REDO IT.** iter156 measured mermaidDialectGap's homework; iter157 swept the other six and wrote what it found into their bodies (see `phase`). Every embedded *check/find out/see whether* in all seven is now answered, and **what is left in each is a JUDGEMENT, which the loop must not make.** Re-reading the seven for facts is spent ground; the probes are re-runnable if you doubt a number (`.mtk/paths-156/probe-mermaid-surface.py`, `.mtk/paths-157/probe-dead-knob-surface.py`).

**THE LIVE LEAD IS ITER157's COROLLARY, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE ONE JUST EXHAUSTED: FOR EACH DIMENSION OF CLAIM THE DOCS MAKE, IS IT SWEPT TREE-WIDE OR HELD AGAINST ONE FILE?** CLI options ARE swept tree-wide (CliReferencePageTests, ~132 invocations). Config-field promises WERE NOT — that was iter157's find, now closed for the two dead knobs. **Untested dimensions worth the same question:** Confluence label names (README's is checked — is every doc's?), `_meta/` frontmatter field names, the `DOCUME_*` env var names, `docume.json` field names generally (not just the dead two), and the `§`-numbers docs cite at each other. Method: find the assertion, NOT the test class you expect to hold it (see method-notes.md, iter157) — a check named after one file may already guard the tree.

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. TEN BOXES ARE UNCHECKED AND ALL TEN ARE MIRKO'S:** five milestone gates (m2, m3, m4, m5, m6) and five side items (paste-rule-8-2a, paste-force-push-hook, settings-corrections, paste-format-on-edit-hook, restart-loop-driver). **`python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` FAILS IF THE `gates` MIRROR STOPS MATCHING THOSE BOXES, INCLUDING ON STATUS DRIFT** — trust the checker over the prose. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands; iter140 tested what it activates, 9/9, nothing pending), gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance — iter157 measured both its options), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0).

**IF MIRKO ANSWERS planSection5Deviations, THE EDIT IS SIX FILES PER KNOB, NOT THREE, AND A TEST NOW HOLDS YOU TO IT.** `PlanDataContractTests.DeadFields[].Places` carries the measured set and `Every_shipped_artifact_that_names_a_dead_knob_is_recorded` fails in BOTH directions — strike or build in all six and empty or keep `Places` in the same change. The two places nobody had recorded are the SKILL.md input tables (docs-loop:60, docs-refresh:44).

**paste-format-on-edit-hook IS A PURE PASTE — ITS QUESTION IS SETTLED, SO DO NOT RE-ASK IT AND DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`.** `decisions.formatOnEditHook` is "delete", CLOSED, loop's half shipped at iter155. **IF MIRKO HAS PASTED IT** — check that `.claude/settings.json` has no `hooks` key, do not assume; it still had one at iter157 — then `git add -- .claude/settings.json`, commit it, tick that box, move the mirror off PENDING, and archive both the gate item and the paste file. **The loop cannot write `.claude/`**: a path-based classifier sits above the permission layer. Do not retry it and do not route around it with an allowlisted `python3`.

**SEVEN DECISIONS ARE STILL OPEN, ALL MIRKO'S, ALL NOW FULLY MEASURED:** mermaidDialectGap, m5Acceptance, pushPolicy, planSection5Deviations, planSection6Deviations, planSection9Deviation, planSection10Deviations.

**IF restart-loop-driver IS TICKED:** re-run `python3 .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py` as the in-situ confirmation and expect cell A to go RED (driver now NEWER than the commit), with the next log line carrying `(pass N)` and `[model: ...]` and the log file named `iter-<n>-pass<NNNN>-<ts>.log`. **NO CODE CHANGE IS PENDING** — iter140 tested every function the restart wakes, 9/9. Expect ONE cosmetic change: `modelUsage` will read `claude-opus-5` instead of `claude-opus-5[1m]`, same canonicalModel / contextWindow / maxOutputTokens (measured).

**READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH tools/loop/docume-loop.sh.** It is the one file an iteration can edit but cannot make take effect: the running driver started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once. So check whether your 'fix' is already there and simply not running — as of iter140 the committed version is TESTED, so the prior is strongly that it is already correct. Live despite the staleness, because they are re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md and loop-settings.json.

**HYGIENE, NOT URGENT, AND DO NOT DELETE IT WITHOUT ASKING:** `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json` is untracked and was created 2026-07-24 20:31 by an MTK analytics write that ran with `tests/golden` as its cwd. It is a data file, so the global rule says ask before removing. It breaks nothing today (the suite is 1389/1389 with it present, and the prose sweeps exclude `tests/`), but `tests/golden/` is a rule §4.3 contract directory and a stray `.claude/` inside it is a trap for any future golden enumerator. Ask Mirko whether to delete it or gitignore it.

decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is still his; the FACTS were measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else. Options unchanged: (a) upgrade-or-replace, (b) strip a trailing `;` in tools/render-mermaid.mjs, (c) report unsupported dialects as a named degradation instead of failing the page. **What iter156 added, and (1) kills half of (a):** (1) **NO LATER VERSION EXISTS** — 1.1.3 is `dist-tags.latest`, ten published, time.modified 2026-02-26, so (a) means REPLACE or nothing; the "check whether a later version takes `graph TD;` and `pie`" homework in the gate has been deleted because it is answered. (2) **THE GAP IS 17 TYPES, NOT 1** — 10/10 spellings of graph/flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, stateDiagram/-v2 and xychart-beta render; 0 of 18 other mermaid v11 spellings do (pie, gantt, journey, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, quadrantChart, requirementDiagram, C4Context, sankey-beta, block-beta, packet-beta, kanban, architecture-beta, radar-beta, treemap-beta, zenuml). Closed by construction: detectDiagramType (index.ts:54) has four branches + a flowchart default, parseMermaid (parser.ts:31) adds state diagrams. (3) **THE SEMICOLON IS AN INCONSISTENCY INSIDE THE LIBRARY, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES (b) CHEAP** — detectDiagramType splits on /[\n;]/ and ALREADY tolerates it (sequenceDiagram; classDiagram; erDiagram; xychart-beta; render), parseMermaid re-splits on \n alone so the ";" reaches the flowchart header regex's \s*$ (parser.ts:44) and graph TD; flowchart LR; graph TB; stateDiagram; stateDiagram-v2; fail. 9/9 predicted from source. (4) **NEW: YAML FRONTMATTER FAILS ON EVERY TYPE INCLUDING THE SIX THAT WORK** (Invalid mermaid header: "---"), 4/4 — mermaid v10+ standard, GitHub renders it, and **no option above addresses it**, so fold it into whichever you pick. Full write-up: GATES.md's mermaid block. Probes: .mtk/paths-156/probe-mermaid-surface.py (39 dialects) and probe-semicolon-mechanism.py (13/13). Historical body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.

doneArchive.format: JSONL, one {"n": <1-based LINE index>, "entry": <string|object>} per line, oldest first. **BOTH ENTRY SHAPES ARE LIVE and any reader must handle both** (counted iter136): 108 strings naming themselves in a leading `iterNNN`, 29 objects carrying `{"iteration": NNN, ...}`. **`n` IS NOT THE ITERATION NUMBER** - see howToAppend.
doneArchive.why: `done` grew to 397 KB of a 459 KB state.json, which put the file over the Read tool's 256 KB ceiling and broke step 1 of the iteration protocol ('Read tools/loop/state.json'). Split at iter127. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED - the archive holds every entry verbatim and the migration asserted the round-trip before rewriting this file.
doneArchive.howToRead: This is history, not orientation - do not read it whole. **USE `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py --find <iteration>`, NOT `grep`.** Measured at iter136 over all 135 iterations, a bare `grep -n 'iterNNN'` is WRONG FOR 27 OF THEM: nothing at all for the object-shaped entries, and for 24 more only lines belonging to some OTHER entry that cites that iteration in prose - which looks exactly like a hit. `--find` resolves both entry shapes and lists prose mentions separately. Forensics: method-notes.md, 'Reading the loop's own history back'. For a range, Read with offset/limit (one entry per line); `tail -3` still works.
doneArchive.howToAppend: EVERY ITERATION: append one line to the archive with n = doneCount + 1 and bump doneCount. **DO NOT WRITE TO `doneRecent` - IT WAS DRAINED AT ITER151 AND STAYS EMPTY** (see `doneRecentNote`; the archive is the record, and refilling it re-spends the budget four iterations in a row had to scramble for). The trim history below is why. It was 5 until iter128 (which measured 8.5 KB in five entries against a state file that had to shed 27 KB), then 3, then 2; iter129 took it to 1 when the budget check tripped on its own prose and two long entries no longer fit. THE PATTERN IS THE POINT: the iteration that grows this file pays it back, rather than raising the budget to suit itself. ASSERT THE ENTRY YOU DROP IS ALREADY IN THE ARCHIVE before dropping it, and run `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` afterwards. THE ARCHIVE IS AUTHORITATIVE AND COMPLETE; doneRecent is a convenience tail and nothing more. If a condensed entry is what fits inline, condense it in BOTH places so the duplication stays verbatim. **`n` IS A LINE INDEX, NOT AN ITERATION NUMBER** (iter136): iter48 logged twice, so `n = iteration + 1` from n=50 on. Do NOT 'repair' that by renumbering. check-state-size.py now also checks ATTRIBUTION, COVERAGE and HEAD - the last would have caught iter132's loss when it happened.
doneArchive.note: doneRecent DUPLICATES the newest archive lines on purpose (inline context for a cold session). The archive is authoritative; doneCount counts the archive, not doneRecent.
